subject: Re: Aperture — request pattern details + recommended GPU pool and reserved commit
messages:
From: Maria Chu <maria.chu@aperturehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aperturehealth.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing question: expected throughput & commitments for dedicated GPU pool

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for last week's call — the team asked me to share a short sample of our production traffic (attached workload_sample.csv) and lay out our expectations so we can get a proposal that maps to real usage. Key details: 
- Expected steady-state: ~120 requests/sec across our primary API (chat + summarization).
- Peak: short spikes up to ~380 req/sec (5–10 minute windows).
- Average input tokens: 420; average generated tokens: 160 (so ~580 tokens per request).
- Concurrency target: p95 concurrent requests ~95.
- Model mix: 70% medium-gen (13B) for sync responses, 30% heavy-gen (70B) for longer multi-turn summaries.
- SLA ask: p95 latency for sync flows under 400ms.
- Compliance: SOC2 requirement and isolated tenant pool for PHI flows.

We'd like: 1) a recommended GPU pool size with rationale, 2) reserved commit pricing for 12-month and 24-month options, 3) burst/credit model for peaks, and 4) any constraints/assumptions (e.g., quantization, max context).

Attached is a small CSV sample (1 day) and a short reqs-by-hour sheet in aperture_requirements.xlsx. Happy to hop on a quick follow-up if it helps.

Best,
Maria Chu
Head of Product Integrations
Aperture Health

Attachment: workload_sample.csv (CSV, 42KB)

Hi Maria — thanks for the data, that helps a lot. Quick clarifying Qs before we size:
- Are the heavy-gen (70B) requests primarily async batch jobs or live sync flows that need p95 latency?
- For multi-turn sessions, what fraction of requests include a long context (>2k tokens)?
- Do you have any hard memory constraints (must be fit on 40GB cards) or preference for H100 vs A100 hardware?

Karthik is on the thread to provide a first-pass GPU pool recommendation based on the CSV. If it's easier, we can do a 30-min sizing call later today.

Separately, I'll draft a 12/24-month reserved commit outline with burst credits and expected per-token economics and share it as a PDF.

Thanks —

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Chu <maria.chu@aperturehealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing question: recommended GPU pool + assumptions (first pass)

Hi Maria — I pulled the CSV and ran a quick throughput model. Summary of assumptions and a conservative recommendation below so we have something concrete to iterate on: 

Assumptions made from your sample:
- Avg tokens per request: 580 (420 in, 160 out).
- Token generation throughput per GPU: ~1,200 tokens/sec for a quantized 13B on A100-40 (when using batching); ~350 tokens/sec for a quantized 70B on A100-80 (estimate depends on kernel mix).
- 70/30 model split (13B/70B).
- We assume active KV caching for multi-turn sessions reduces compute for repeated prefixes by ~20% (depends on session reuse).
- Target p95 latency budget: 400ms. We budget 300ms for model generation to leave headroom for network and parsing.

Sizing math (rounded):
- Effective per-request token-work: 580 tokens. At 300ms generation window, that implies ~1,933 tokens/sec per concurrent slot (580 / 0.3).
- For 13B: each A100-40 can sustain ~1,200 tok/sec → ~0.62 concurrent slots per GPU for 13B.
- For 70B: each A100-80 can sustain ~350 tok/sec → ~0.18 concurrent slots per GPU for 70B.

Translate to capacity for p95 concurrency 95 with 70/30 split:
- Concurrent 13B slots needed: 0.7 * 95 ≈ 67 slots → GPUs required (13B): 67 / 0.62 ≈ 108 A100-40 equivalent GPUs.
- Concurrent 70B slots needed: 0.3 * 95 ≈ 28 slots → GPUs required (70B): 28 / 0.18 ≈ 156 A100-80 equivalent GPUs.

This raw calculation is conservative and intentionally overprovisions because:
- We assumed no batching efficiency beyond steady-state batching; in practice, batching and dynamic packing often improve token/sec by 20–40% depending on request alignment.
- Quantization and using H100 optimizations can materially reduce GPU count for the 70B class.

Recommendations (practical flavors):
1) Pilot (recommended first step) — Mixed pool, 6 H100-80GB + 18 A100-40GB with autoscaled burst to cloud-hosted capacity. Rationale: gives a baseline for 24/7 low-latency traffic and lets us gather live batching efficiencies. Expected steady-state coverage ~20–30% of your peak p95 concurrent need but should deliver very low latencies for most requests.
2) Production reserved commit — If you want an on-prem/dedicated pool to cover p95 without external bursting, we'd recommend sizing to 70% of the conservative raw calc (to account for expected batching gains and caching): 
   - 13B class: ~75 A100-40GB equivalents
   - 70B class: ~110 A100-80GB equivalents
   -> A hybrid flavor using H100s where possible could reduce the 70B count by ~30% (so ~75 H100-80GB).
3) Pricing/commit options: 12-month reserved commit with 20% discount, 24-month with 30% discount. Burst credits: allow 25% burst capacity (metered) above commit with a reduced overage uplift.

Folks — I know those raw GPU numbers look large. The two levers that materially alter them are: model quantization & use of H100 (or other newer generation hardware), and accepting a small number of p95 latency SLO breaches covered by cross-region fallback to hosted models. I'd recommend the Pilot first to measure real-world batching and token-level ceilings.

Happy to jump on a sizing workshop with your infra team if you want a deeper run.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: procurement@aperturehealth.com <procurement@aperturehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aperture — request pattern details + recommended GPU pool and reserved commit

Hi Grace / Karthik,

Thanks for the detailed sizing and the PDF draft (we've reviewed redwood_draft_offer.pdf). A few commercial questions from Procurement: 
- Aperture is comfortable with a 12-month commit to start but we'd like a discount floor of 22% for a 12-month guaranteed commit (your draft shows 20%).
- For burst credits: can you confirm an automatic burst of at least 20% capacity without prior approval and a defined overage rate?
- Can you include a 90-day ramp clause in the contract so we can convert pilot telemetry to final commit numbers without penalty?

On the technical side, a couple of clarifications for Karthik: 
- We plan to convert most 70B workloads to 8-bit quantized variants — are your 70B performance numbers in the draft assuming int8/4 quantization?
- We will need a SOC2 scoping addendum prior to signing.

If you can respond to the discount & burst language, and we can get a DocuSign-ready quote, Procurement can turn fast.

Thanks,
Aperture Procurement
